clue.text: Player lacking finesse through cramp

parts.note: a ham is an actor who overplays without subtlety
per means through or by way of, as in per post

explanation.surface: A clumsy footballer is struck down by cramp mid-match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cramp' is the verb here, to restrict or hinder, not the muscle spasm the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To cramp someone's style is to restrict or impede it, the same as to hold it back.

clue.text: Flowers rise up, captured by artist

indicators.note: captured by says the first piece is held inside the artist's name

parts.note: Frans Hals was the Dutch portrait painter of the Laughing Cavalier
to rebel is to rise up against authority

explanation.surface: A painter imprisons the rebels who rose up, among the flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Harebells are small blue bell-shaped wild flowers, an example of the class.

clue.text: Priest our group supports weekly?

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: a weekly is a magazine, shortened to mag
us means our group, the speakers

explanation.surface: A clergyman asks whether our group is propping up a weekly paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supports' puts US below MAG in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A magus is one of the Zoroastrian priestly caste of ancient Persia, the Magi.

clue.text: Soldiers bound by duty drive away

indicators.note: bound by says the soldiers are held within the word for duty

parts.note: excise is a tax or duty on goods
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Troops tied to their duty are ordered to drive off the enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive away' means expel an evil spirit, not the soldiers' manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: To exorcise is to expel or drive out an evil spirit by ritual.

clue.text: Glass earlier broken by companion

indicators.note: broken by says the word for earlier is split open with the companion inside

parts.note: sooner means earlier, as in the sooner the better
CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: A glass gets smashed earlier by a drinking companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a tall glass for sherry or, in Australia, beer.

clue.text: Man going after solution, endlessly in bind, showing spirit

indicators.note: going after says the man's letters are placed at the end
in says the shortened word sits inside the word for bind

parts.note: cement is something that binds things together

indicators.note: endlessly says the word for solution loses its final letter

parts.note: a remedy is a solution to a problem
he stands for a man

explanation.surface: A man follows a solution, stuck in a bind, and turns to drink for courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly', 'in' and 'going after' build the drink; 'spirit' is the liqueur, not the courage the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Creme de menthe is a peppermint liqueur, and spirit is used loosely here for an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Revolutionary ace in utterance to grab attention permitting no U-turn

indicators.note: in says the first two pieces sit inside the cry

parts.note: oy is a cry used to attract someone's notice
new and revolutionary both mean radically novel
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A radical champion is heard shouting for attention, refusing to back down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests a reversal, but it simply means NEW.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-way street lets traffic travel in only one direction, so turning back is barred.

clue.text: Fanatic in riot tossed food

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast or fanatic, as in a fitness nut

indicators.note: tossed says the letters of in riot are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A fanatic at a riot hurls food around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossed' rearranges IN RIOT into RITION.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutrition is nourishment, the food a body takes in.

clue.text: Love getting about around river

indicators.note: around says the word for about wraps the endearment

parts.note: re means about or concerning
hon, short for honey, is a term of endearment like love

explanation.surface: Love is getting about all around the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link: love takes 'about' around itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhone is a major river running from Switzerland through France to the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Rally run by revolutionary clear about first of objectives

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: about says the turned word goes around the next letter
revolutionary says the word for clear turns right round

parts.note: to purge is to clear out

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of objectives

explanation.surface: A revolutionary purge, run around its first objective, sparks a rally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns PURGE into EGRUP, which goes 'about' O, the 'first of' objectives.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally and to regroup both mean to reassemble forces for a fresh effort.

clue.text: Upper edge, in potty or cup, royal blue?

indicators.note: in says the edge goes inside the scrambled letters
potty means crazy, so the letters of or cup royal are scrambled

parts.note: the rim is the upper edge of a cup or bowl

explanation.surface: A gilded rim on a potty or cup in royal blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potty' rearranges OR CUP ROYAL into PARYCOLOUR, and 'in' puts RIM inside it. 'royal' looks part of royal blue but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue is one of the three primary colours of paint, an example of the class, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Singled out line heard in funky music

parts.note: elect means chosen or singled out

indicators.note: heard says the word for line is taken by its sound

parts.note: a row is a line of things

explanation.surface: A singled-out line of lyrics is heard in a funk track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' gives RO, which sounds like ROW.
explanation.definitionFit: Electro is a style of electronic dance music grown out of funk.

clue.text: Simple objective of student accurately quoted

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a degree a student aims for
sic is written after a quotation to show it is reproduced exactly

explanation.surface: A student's simple aim is quoted word for word.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic and simple both describe something elementary and uncomplicated.

clue.text: Appeal, day before festival, to catch renegade, one repeated

parts.note: it means sex appeal

indicators.note: to catch says the eve holds the next pieces inside

parts.note: an eve is the day before a festival, as in Christmas Eve
a rat is a deserter or renegade
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An appeal goes out the day before the festival to catch a renegade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appeal' is IT in the old sense of sex appeal; 'to catch' does the containing.
explanation.definitionFit: Iterative describes a process done over and over, each step a repetition.

clue.text: Inactive person subsequently embracing occupational therapy and exercise

indicators.note: embracing says the word for subsequently wraps the other pieces

parts.note: later means subsequently
to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: A layabout later takes up occupational therapy and exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' signals the containment; the Lotus-eaters of Homer's Odyssey idled away their days.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotus-eaters in the Odyssey lost all ambition, so the term means an idle, dreamy person.

clue.text: Take time over organised display

parts.note: ran means organised, as in ran the event
to sport something is to wear or display it

explanation.surface: Take time over an organised show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a link: T sits above the rest in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport goods is to take or carry them from place to place.

clue.text: Snake trade?

definitions.meaning: to move in a twisting course, as a snake or a road does
the trade is a steady ... blowing towards the equator

explanation.definitionFit: Wind is both a verb for twisting progress and the noun naming the trades, those steady tropical winds.

clue.text: Social clubs to charge for qualification

parts.note: a do is a party or social event
C is the card abbreviation for clubs
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: Social clubs set a charge for membership qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctorate is the highest academic degree, a qualification such as a PhD.

clue.text: A sect in unsettled area spread over America

indicators.note: unsettled says the letters of A sect in are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A religious sect is restless in a region extending across America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettled' rearranges A SECT IN into ESTANCI. 'spread' is a noun, a large ranch.
explanation.definitionFit: An estancia is a cattle ranch in Spanish-speaking South America, and spread is slang for a ranch.

clue.text: Right to have friends round

indicators.note: round says the word for friends is turned to read the other way

parts.note: pals are friends

explanation.surface: Is it right to have friends round?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' is the adverb, as in right or slap in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap as an adverb means directly or exactly, as in slap bang in the centre.

clue.text: Individual in charge, initially timid, losing head very fast

indicators.note: initially says this piece comes at the front
losing head says the word for timid drops its first letter

parts.note: shy means timid
a person is an individual

explanation.surface: A timid person in charge loses their head and moves very fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' cuts SHY to HY, and 'initially' puts it first.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypersonic speed is more than five times the speed of sound, extremely fast.

clue.text: Large number light up? Doctor accepts that

indicators.note: accepts says the doctor takes the turned word inside

parts.note: MD is a doctor of medicine

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: airy means light, as in an airy room

explanation.surface: Lots light up when a doctor accepts that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' signals reversal in a down light; 'accepts' does the containing and 'that' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A myriad is a countless host, and originally ten thousand.

clue.text: Spots you cultivated around fine hedge

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters go round the fine letter
cultivated says the letters of Spots you are worked into a new form

parts.note: F is the pencil abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A gardener notices you have trimmed around a fine hedge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivated' rearranges SPOTS YOU into PUSSYOOT, with F placed inside. 'hedge' is the verb, to be evasive.
explanation.definitionFit: To pussyfoot is to act timidly and avoid committing, the same as to hedge.

clue.text: Insects quietly settling on parts of our plates at regular intervals

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece settling on another sits above it

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

indicators.note: at regular intervals picks every second letter of our plates

explanation.surface: Insects quietly settle on parts of our dinner plates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts of' is a link; every other letter of OUR PLATES gives UPAE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupae are insects in the stage between larva and adult, as plural nouns.

clue.text: Trouble coming from ragtag group

indicators.note: coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A scruffy gang is the source of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang for aggressive trouble or hassle.

clue.text: Range that's great, full of charm, with 50% off

indicators.note: full of says the great letters wrap the halved charm

parts.note: GT is the abbreviation for great

indicators.note: with 50% off says the word for charm loses its second half

parts.note: an amulet is a charm worn for protection

explanation.surface: A great range, full of charm, now half price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with 50% off' halves the six-letter charm; 'full of' does the containing.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamut is the whole range of something, from the musical scale.

clue.text: Condition mostly cooler? Nothing against going inside

indicators.note: going inside says the last two pieces enter the shortened word
mostly says the word for cooler loses its last letter

parts.note: the cooler is slang for prison
O is zero, nothing
V for versus means against

explanation.surface: A fridge mostly works on condition there is nothing against it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooler' is slang for prison, not a fridge; 'mostly' cuts it to PRISO, and O and V go 'inside'.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a condition attached to an agreement.

clue.text: Plan one brought about, receiving constant tributes

indicators.note: receiving says the turned letters take in the constant
brought about says the plan and the one are turned to read the other way

parts.note: to aim is to plan or intend
taken as written
C is the scientific symbol for a constant such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: A plan is brought about, earning constant praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought about' turns both pieces as one run, giving ENOMIA, which 'receiving' wraps around the constant.
explanation.definitionFit: Encomia is the plural of encomium, a formal expression of high praise.

clue.text: City name covering majority of untypical outer part

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London

indicators.note: covering says the word for name wraps the shortened piece

parts.note: a term is a word or name for something

indicators.note: majority of says the word for untypical drops its last letter

parts.note: odd means untypical

explanation.surface: A city name covers most of what is unusual about the outskirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'majority of' cuts ODD to OD, which TERM is 'covering'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ectoderm is the outermost cell layer of an embryo, its outer part.

clue.text: Action shattered tablet

indicators.note: shattered says the word tablet is broken and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone acts and the tablet is shattered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattered' rearranges TABLET into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle is a fight, a military action.
